newsitem.title: FRANCE: French direct mail mogul on trial for deceit.
newsitem.headline: French direct mail mogul on trial for deceit.

text.p: A prosecutor asked a French court on Thursday to sentence a direct mail mogul to a 15-month suspended jail term for allegedly selling useless gadgets and failing to deliver on promises of enticing prizes.
He told Bernard Graeff, 48, chairman of France Direct Service (FDS) and other companies: "You became rich on the backs of people with little means and you stole their dreams as well."
Prosecutor Guy Robert also requested a 200,000-franc ($40,000) fine for Graeff who is on trial on charges including deceit and misuse of corporate funds.
Robert contended Graeff had "promised fabulous gains through various games in order to sell goods which were mostly poor-quality imported gadgets".

Graeff is accused of leading customers to believe they would automatically win cars or exotic holidays if they ordered goods. Some received a pocket gadget closer to a stapler than to the sewing machine they had expected.
Many of the gadgets paid for were never delivered at all as stocks ran out, the court was told.
